title: story-080's declared drift guard between mainnet-addresses.ts and the regenerated ContractAddresses interface does not exist, and the two files already disagree
severityRationale: No runtime consequence in this repo — mainnet-addresses.ts is a hand-maintained copy-out artifact and nothing in-tree reads it. But `dev` REGENERATES the interface every run, so the one thing standing between a silent key-set drift and a broken downstream UI is a check the story claims to have performed and that no tool can perform.
faithfulness: Story-080 acceptance, ticked: 'Confirm `tsc` passes — the `: ContractAddresses` annotation on `mainnetAddresses` is the only drift guard between the two files.' Autonomous Decision 6 honestly records that it was NOT run because no tsconfig.json exists. The honesty is creditable; the ticked box is not met, and the story's own statement that this is 'the only drift guard' means there is now no drift guard at all.
description: `npm run dev` regenerates server/deployments/addresses.ts (the ContractAddresses interface) on every run via server/generate-ts-addresses.js:63. The hand-maintained server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts must satisfy that interface. There is no tsconfig.json anywhere outside node_modules, so nothing type-checks it. Comparing the two key sets today: all 56 interface keys are present in mainnet-addresses.ts (the direction that would be a hard tsc error is clean), but mainnet-addresses.ts carries three keys — BurnerEYE, BurnerFlax, BurnerSCX — that the interface does not declare, which TypeScript's excess-property checking on a typed object literal would reject. The guard the story leans on would therefore fail today if it existed.
failureScenario: A future story adds or removes a `_trackDeployment` call in DeployMocks — exactly what story-080 did when it dropped StableStaker and added Antimatter and StableStakerV2. The next `npm run dev` regenerates addresses.ts with the new key set. Nobody updates the hand-maintained mainnet-addresses.ts, because the story's stated safety net is `tsc` and no tsconfig.json exists for `tsc` to act on. The repo's CI (forge fmt --check, forge build --sizes, forge test) has nothing to say about TypeScript. The drift surfaces later, in a downstream UI project that copies both files in and fails to build, or worse reads a key that silently resolves to undefined.
impact: A future `_trackDeployment` addition or removal in DeployMocks silently re-shapes the interface that mainnet-addresses.ts is annotated against, and nothing catches it until a downstream UI build breaks. This delta already exercised that path (StableStaker removed, Antimatter and StableStakerV2 added).
evidence:
`find <project>/work -maxdepth 2 -name 'tsconfig*.json' -not -path './node_modules/*'` -> no results. Key-set comparison script over addresses.ts / mainnet-addresses.ts / local-addresses.ts:
  interface keys: 56 | mainnet keys: 59 | local keys: 56
  IN INTERFACE, MISSING FROM mainnet-addresses.ts: []
  IN mainnet-addresses.ts, NOT IN INTERFACE: ['BurnerEYE', 'BurnerFlax', 'BurnerSCX']
  interface-vs-local delta: []
recommendation: Add a minimal tsconfig.json covering server/deployments/*.ts with `strict: true`, and either declare the three Burner* keys on ContractAddresses (by adding their `_trackDeployment` calls, the codegen path story-080 itself insists on) or drop them from mainnet-addresses.ts. Then wire `tsc --noEmit` into the same GitHub workflow that already runs `forge fmt --check` / `forge build --sizes` / `forge test`, so the guard is enforced rather than asserted.

classification.assetImpact: None in this repo. mainnet-addresses.ts is a hand-maintained copy-out artifact and nothing in-tree reads it.
attackPath: No attacker. Silent-drift path, whose first leg has ALREADY OCCURRED:
1. A story adds or removes a _trackDeployment call in DeployMocks - exactly what story-080 did (StableStaker removed; Antimatter and StableStakerV2 added).
2. `npm run dev` regenerates server/deployments/addresses.ts with the new key set on every run.
3. Nobody updates the hand-maintained mainnet-addresses.ts, because the stated safety net is `tsc` and no tsconfig.json exists.
4. CI (forge fmt --check, forge build --sizes, forge test) has nothing to say about TypeScript.
5. The drift surfaces later in a downstream UI build - or worse, a key silently resolves to undefined at runtime.
classification.likelihood: the drift itself is ALREADY REAL (three undeclared keys, verified this run); the downstream breakage is prospective and out-of-repo.
classification.assumptions: A downstream consumer copies both files in and relies on the annotation.
classification.externalRequirements: An out-of-repo consumer project - which is why this cannot be rated above Low from inside this repo.

classifierJustification: Low CONFIRMED. This is the stronger of the two Law-2 items because its drift is DEMONSTRATED rather than hypothetical - three keys already disagree - so it is not 'speculation on future code'. It is nonetheless held at Low, not Medium: nothing in this repository reads mainnet-addresses.ts, so there is no in-scope function or availability impact, and the only harmed party is an out-of-repo consumer whose existence is an external requirement. The false-assurance channel is present in a mild form (the story asserts a guard that cannot run) but it certifies a TypeScript key-set, not a mainnet cutover, so it does not carry the run-28 Medium weight.
caveatsForHuman: Do NOT collapse with F-03 (DEDUP-29-03) - see that entry's caveat.
Distinct from ledger 98e727214903 (L-07, de-tracked seed artifact): adjacent file family only, different defect.

The recommendation has a dependency worth honouring in order: declaring the three Burner* keys via their _trackDeployment calls is the codegen path story-080 itself insists on; dropping them from mainnet-addresses.ts is the alternative. Adding tsconfig.json WITHOUT resolving the three keys first will turn a silent drift into a red CI on the first run.
